The manipulation of time in this short story is exceptionally well-balanced because it relies on a "real-time" dramatic scene where the "story time" closely matches the "real-world time" it takes to read it. By avoiding artificial stretching or compression within the immediate scene—letting the conversation unfold beat by beat with brief, deliberate actions like feeling under the table or turning a coffee cup—the writer creates a palpable sense of quiet tension and hesitation between the two characters. 

At the same time, the story masterfully compresses years of shared history and time apart into single, loaded lines of dialogue (referencing the sanded-down table, the notch underneath, and how Jakob used to take his coffee). The final exchange about the Sunday bus schedule effectively anchors the pacing, signaling a shift from a brief, guarded encounter to an extended stay, making the temporal flow feel completely natural and emotionally resonant.
